questions: gc1
Which scale keeps groups distinguishable for colour-blind readers and in greyscale?
`scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1")`
`scale_colour_viridis_d()`
`scale_colour_hue()`
`scale_colour_manual(values = c("red", "green"))`
viridis changes lightness as well as hue, so it survives greyscale printing and red-green colour blindness; Set1 and the default hue scale do not.
gc2
SBP change ranges from −20 to +20 mmHg, and 0 means no change. Which colour scale fits?
`scale_colour_gradient(low = "white")`
`scale_colour_viridis_d()`
`scale_colour_gradient2(midpoint = 0)`
`scale_colour_grey(start = 0.2)`
A diverging scale with its neutral colour at a meaningful midpoint shows the direction and size of change.
gc3
Which `theme()` setting removes the minor grid lines?
`panel.grid.minor = element_line()`
`panel.background = element_rect()`
`legend.position = "none"`
`panel.grid.minor = element_blank()`
element_blank() removes a theme element; element_line() and element_rect() style it.
gc4
How do you apply a house theme to every later plot in a report?
Add the theme to the first plot only
Call `theme_set()` once at the start
Save the theme with `ggsave()`
Put the theme inside `aes()`
theme_set() changes the default theme for the rest of the session or document.
gd1
You write `geom_smooth()` before `geom_point()`. What changes?
The line is drawn on top of the points
The points are drawn on top of the line
ggplot2 refuses to draw the two layers
The points take the colour of the line
Layers are drawn in the order they are added: later layers sit on top.
gd2
Why read data with `read_excel("data/bp.xlsx")` rather than `"C:/Users/..."`?
Relative paths load the file faster
The code then runs on another computer
Excel files need a relative path
Absolute paths are not allowed in a Quarto file
A path relative to the project folder works wherever the project is copied; an absolute path only works on your machine.
gd3
ggplot2 has no mosaic geom. Which of these draws a mosaic plot?
`geom_violin()` with a fill
`coord_flip()` on a pie chart
`productplots::prodplot(..., mosaic())`
`facet_wrap()` on a stacked histogram of counts
prodplot() with mosaic() draws a mosaic with ggplot2; base R has mosaicplot(), and ggmosaic is another option once it supports ggplot2 4.
gd4
Why should a figure not rely on colour alone to separate groups?
Colour makes the file too large to share
Some readers cannot tell the colours apart
ggplot2 limits a plot to three colours
Colour slows down rendering of the plot a lot
About 1 in 12 men has a colour-vision deficiency, and figures are often printed in greyscale: add shape, labels or line type.
pa1
36 months of dengue counts should be split into trend, season and noise. Which method does that?
A cartogram
STL decomposition
Parallel coordinates
Community detection
STL (seasonal-trend decomposition by loess) separates a series into trend, seasonal and remainder components.
pa2
Which plot makes a regression's coefficients easy to compare with zero?
A 3D density surface
A hexagon tile map
A forest (coefficient) plot
A Sankey diagram of terms
A forest plot shows each estimate with its confidence interval next to a reference line at 0.
pa3
A cartogram resizes each block by its population. What does it show better than a normal map?
The exact borders of each block
Where the people are, not the land
The road distance to each clinic
The shape of each block's outline
Areas proportional to population show where the people (and so most cases) are; large empty blocks no longer dominate.
pr1
Why use `colors = "bw"` and `theme_bw()` for the journal figure?
Colour figures cannot be saved as TIFF
It stays readable when printed in greyscale
It makes the confidence intervals narrower
ggeffects needs it to compute predictions
Many journals print in black and white; a figure that does not depend on colour reads the same in print.
pr2
Fifty clinics each need the same weekly report. Which approach does the deck use?
Fifty copies of the report, edited by hand
A parameterised template rendered per site
One long report with all sites on every page
A Shiny app that e-mails a screenshot weekly
One template with a site parameter, rendered in a loop, gives consistent reports and one place to fix mistakes.
pr3
Clinicians must filter patients and change the view themselves. Which tool fits?
A static PDF report
A Shiny app
A TIFF figure at 600 dpi
A printed Table 1
Shiny apps run R code in response to the user's inputs, so the reader can change the analysis, not just look at it.
ia1
In `ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")`, what does the tooltip argument do?
Adds a text label beside each point
Shows only the text aesthetic on hover
Turns the axis titles into links
Exports the plot as a text file on disk
tooltip = "text" limits the hover label to the text aesthetic you built; the default lists every mapped aesthetic.
ia2
Your paper goes to a journal as a PDF. What about the interactive plotly figure?
It is converted to an animation in the PDF
It needs a static version for the PDF
It works if the reader opens the PDF online
It is printed with all the tooltips shown
htmlwidgets work in HTML only: put a static figure in the paper and the interactive one in a web supplement.
ia3
What does crosstalk's `SharedData` let you do?
Share a plot on social media from the page
Store the data on a server for other users
Link widgets so a selection filters the others
Speed up a plot by sharing memory between widgets
Widgets built on the same SharedData object respond to each other's selections, in a static page without a server.
db1
"Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data". What usually causes it?
A missing library(ggplot2) call at the top
A vector in aes() not as long as the data
A theme that is applied twice to the plot
Too many rows in the data for ggplot2
Something mapped in aes() has a different length from the data frame, often a vector from outside the data; put it in the data as a column.
db2
What is the first step of layer-by-layer debugging?
Re-install ggplot2 from CRAN and restart the R session
Draw the base plot, then add one layer at a time
Save the plot as a PDF and look at it closely
Switch every geom to geom_point() first
Adding one layer at a time shows exactly which layer breaks the plot.
db3
A plot of 2 million points takes minutes to draw. Which fix helps most?
Add a theme with fewer grid lines
Summarise or bin first (e.g. geom_hex)
Increase the dpi of the saved file
Switch the colour palette to viridis_c
Drawing millions of points is slow and hides density anyway; binning or summarising draws far fewer shapes.
ae1
You need the same plot for each of 12 districts. What is the cleanest approach?
Copy the plot code 12 times and edit each copy
A loop or map() over districts with ggsave()
Facet the plot and save it 12 times
Save one PDF and split it by hand later
A loop or map() writes one file per district from one piece of code, with the file name built from the district.
ae2
Why use a Cairo (or ragg) device for PNG output?
Smaller vector files for printing
Better anti-aliasing and font rendering
Automatic alt text for the figure
Higher statistical precision of the plot
Cairo and ragg draw smoother lines and text and handle fonts consistently across operating systems.
ae3
A journal wants Figure 1 as two panels tagged A and B, 18 cm wide. Which tools fit?
facet_wrap() and then a screenshot of the window
Two separate PNGs pasted together in Word
patchwork with tag_levels, then ggsave(units = "cm")
par(mfrow) with the default device size
patchwork combines ggplots and adds panel tags; ggsave() sets the exact size, units and dpi.
